summary: Backend+frontend testing of Rentabilité CareerOS admin finance dashboard. 13/13 backend pytest tests pass (auth, month summary, 6-month history, past-month zero platform costs, save+recalc with correct gross/adjustments/net/platform conversion/margin, invalid month 422, settings fx/pricing update, members list, 404 on unknown member, paid toggle affects count, AI usage logging via /api/generate SSE, providers list). Frontend admin login + Rentabilité CareerOS tab + all required data-testid elements present (kpi-revenue/platform/ai/margin/active, finance-answers/chart/revenue/costs/ai-buckets/ai-providers/per-member/alerts/projections, projection-100/500/1000, finance-members, finance-month, finance-edit-btn). Editor sheet opens, price/adjustment/cost/fx changes save and refresh KPIs (margin went 317.62 -> 317.40 when fx 1.37 -> 1.40 then restored). Mobile 390px: no horizontal page overflow (scrollWidth == innerWidth 390). Activité tab default content (stat cards, LLM split) still works.

issues: Recharts emits width(-1)/height(-1) console warnings on first render — chart renders fine after mount but a minWidth/minHeight on the ResponsiveContainer wrapper would eliminate the warning.

Playwright reported Sheet bounding box x=1913, width=576 (extending past 1920 viewport). Visually the Sheet still renders readable content via animation, but at exactly 1920 viewport the right edge is clipped on some browsers. Not blocking — real users can scroll horizontally within sheet; buttons triggered via JS click. May be a shadcn Sheet transform-animation measurement artifact.

action_items: (Optional) Add minWidth/minHeight to FinanceChart ResponsiveContainer to silence recharts warning.

(Note, not a bug) In the current preview DB, paid_override=10 is set on the current month, so toggling an individual member's paid flag correctly does NOT change the 'paid' count (per spec — override wins). Verified the toggle persists via PUT /api/admin/members/{id}/paid, and when paid_override is cleared the count does follow flags (asserted in test_members_toggle_paid_affects_count).
critical_code_review_comments: finance.py is well-structured, uses async properly, excludes _id, validates with Pydantic, parametrizes month regex, computes CAD conversion via fx. Good coverage of edge cases (past-month zero platform, invoice gap_cad/gap_pct, scenario ratio_assumed flag).
AI usage logger is fire-and-forget with exception swallow — correct for non-critical telemetry.
Mark_active uses $setOnInsert upsert — idempotent per month per user, good.
